newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-LOCHER LEADS AFTER FIRST LEG OF GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-LOCHER LEADS AFTER FIRST LEG OF GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Swiss Steve Locher edged compatriot and defending champion Michael Von Gruenigen to take the lead in the opening World Cup giant slalom on Sunday.
Locher clocked 58.56 seconds, 0.59 of a second ahead of Von Gruenigen.
Norwegian Lasse Kjus began his defence of the overall World Cup title by posting the third fastest time of 59.27 on the Rettenbach piste under sunny, blue skies.
Austrians Rainer Salzgeber and Guenther Mader finished fourth and fifth respectively.
Mader, Austria's most consistent skier over the past decade and runner-up in the overall World Cup in 1995 and 1996, had back problems during training last week.
